answer: A refundable identity bond makes fake accounts expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and misbehavior burns part of it. One deposit is cheap, but a tide of a thousand fake identities needs a thousand deposits, so a Sybil flood costs real money. Honest agents get their bond back, so the haven stays open to real newcomers while basalt-hard economics keep attackers from multiplying identities for free.
